checks.title: SQL injection: query built via string formatting
checks.remediation: Use parameterised queries: db.Query("SELECT … WHERE x = ?", value). Never concatenate or fmt.Sprintf user-controlled values into SQL.

checks.title: Command injection: exec.Command with shell wrapper or concatenated argv
checks.remediation: Pass argv as a list rather than going through `sh -c`. If shell semantics are required, sanitise inputs with shellescape or use os/exec with explicit env+argv.

checks.title: Weak hash used for password storage
checks.remediation: Use bcrypt, scrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2 for password hashing. Raw MD5/SHA1 is unsuitable — they're fast hashes with no work factor and no per-record salt.

checks.title: AWS access-key ID literal embedded in source
checks.remediation: Load AWS credentials from the SDK's default chain (env, ~/.aws/credentials, instance role). If this is a real key, rotate it now.

checks.title: eval() with non-literal argument
checks.remediation: Replace eval() with explicit parsing (JSON.parse for JSON, Function constructor with allowlist for templated logic). Eval of user-controlled input is direct RCE.

checks.title: innerHTML assigned from a non-literal expression
checks.remediation: Use textContent (sanitises automatically) or sanitise input through DOMPurify before assignment.

checks.title: child_process.exec with shell semantics
checks.remediation: Prefer child_process.execFile or spawn with argv as an array. exec passes its first argument to a shell.

checks.title: document.write — DOM-based XSS surface
checks.remediation: document.write() is XSS-prone and blocks the parser. Build DOM nodes via createElement/textContent, or use template literals + a sanitiser.

checks.title: require() called with a non-literal path
checks.remediation: Pass a string literal to require(). Dynamic require paths let an attacker load arbitrary modules.

checks.title: AWS access-key ID literal embedded in JavaScript source
checks.remediation: Load credentials from process.env or the AWS SDK's default chain. Rotate the exposed key.

checks.title: Command injection: Runtime.exec / ProcessBuilder with a concatenated argument
checks.remediation: Pass the command + args as a String[] / List<String> of literals; never build a shell string from user input. If a shell is unavoidable, validate against an allowlist.

checks.title: SQL injection: query built by string concatenation
checks.remediation: Use a PreparedStatement with bound `?` parameters: conn.prepareStatement("… WHERE x = ?"). Never concatenate user input into SQL.

checks.title: Weak cryptography: MD5/SHA-1 digest or DES/ECB/RC4 cipher
checks.remediation: Use SHA-256+ for digests and AES-GCM (never ECB/DES/RC4) for encryption. For passwords use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2/PBKDF2.

checks.title: Insecure deserialization: Java ObjectInputStream
checks.remediation: Avoid Java native serialization on untrusted input. Prefer a data format (JSON) with a safe parser, or install an ObjectInputFilter allowlist (JEP 290).

checks.title: XML external entity (XXE): XML parser factory created without hardening
checks.remediation: Disable DOCTYPE/external entities: factory.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true) (or XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING). Prefer a parser that rejects external entities by default.

checks.title: Insecure cookie: Secure/HttpOnly explicitly disabled
checks.remediation: Set cookies Secure + HttpOnly (cookie.setSecure(true); cookie.setHttpOnly(true)). Disable only with a documented reason.

checks.title: Insecure randomness: java.util.Random / Math.random in a security context
checks.remediation: Use java.security.SecureRandom for tokens, salts, session IDs, and keys. java.util.Random / Math.random are statistically predictable.

checks.title: LDAP injection: search filter built by string concatenation
checks.remediation: Escape LDAP filter metacharacters (encodeForLDAP) or use parameterised search; never concatenate user input into a filter.

checks.title: SSRF: outbound request built directly from a request parameter
checks.remediation: Validate the URL against an allowlist of permitted hosts/schemes before the request; never pass a raw request parameter to an HTTP client.

checks.title: Reflected XSS: request value written straight to the servlet response
checks.remediation: HTML-encode untrusted output (OWASP Encoder: Encode.forHtml(...)) or use a context-aware templating engine; never write a raw request parameter to the response.

checks.title: Path traversal: filesystem path built from a request parameter
checks.remediation: Resolve the path against a fixed base directory and verify it stays within it (canonical path + prefix check), or map the request value to an allowlisted file; never pass it straight to a file API.

checks.title: Dockerfile doesn't drop privileges (no USER directive in file)
checks.remediation: Add `USER <non-root>` after package installs. Containers running as UID 0 escalate easily into the host on misconfigured runtimes.

checks.title: Dockerfile uses ADD when COPY would suffice
checks.remediation: Use COPY for local files. If you need a URL, prefer curl + verified checksum in a RUN step.

checks.title: Dockerfile pins to :latest (or no tag at all)
checks.remediation: Pin to a specific tag or digest (e.g. `python:3.11.7-slim` or `python@sha256:…`). `:latest` makes builds unreproducible AND ships unreviewed upstream changes.

checks.title: Dockerfile base image is not pinned to a digest
checks.remediation: Pin the base image by digest: `FROM python:3.14-slim@sha256:…`. Keep the tag alongside it for readability — the digest is what makes the build reproducible, and a tool like Renovate or Dependabot can bump both together.

checks.title: Kubernetes pod runs with privileged: true
checks.remediation: Drop `privileged: true`. If a workload genuinely needs host capabilities, use `securityContext.capabilities.add` with the minimum set.

checks.title: Kubernetes pod uses hostNetwork: true
checks.remediation: hostNetwork: true binds pod ports to the node's network namespace and shares its interfaces. Justify per-workload; default should be false.

checks.title: Kubernetes container allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
checks.remediation: Set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`. Required for compliance with most pod-security policies.

checks.title: Kubernetes container runAsUser: 0 (root)
checks.remediation: Set runAsUser to a non-zero UID, or runAsNonRoot: true to refuse to start if the image's USER is root.

checks.title: Django view '$VIEW' does not use LoginRequiredMixin.
checks.remediation: Django view '$VIEW' does not use LoginRequiredMixin. Add LoginRequiredMixin or @login_required to protect this view.

checks.title: FastAPI route '$FUNC' has no authentication dependency (Depends(...)).
checks.remediation: FastAPI route '$FUNC' has no authentication dependency (Depends(...)). Inject a dependency such as Depends(get_current_user) to enforce auth.

checks.title: Flask route '$FUNC' is missing @login_required decorator.
checks.remediation: Flask route '$FUNC' is missing @login_required decorator. Any user can access this endpoint without authentication.

checks.title: Flask route '$FUNC' has no auth-style decorator (@login_required, @requires_auth, @jwt_required, or @auth.login_required) directly above the @app.route(...) line.
checks.remediation: Flask route '$FUNC' has no auth-style decorator (@login_required, @requires_auth, @jwt_required, or @auth.login_required) directly above the @app.route(...) line. Confirm authentication is enforced.

checks.title: JWT decoded with signature verification disabled.
checks.remediation: JWT decoded with signature verification disabled. This allows an attacker to forge tokens. Remove options={"verify_signature": False} and specify a strong algorithm.

checks.title: Legacy / broken symmetric cipher imported (DES, 3DES, RC4, ARC2, Blowfish).
checks.remediation: Legacy / broken symmetric cipher imported (DES, 3DES, RC4, ARC2, Blowfish). These are no longer considered secure. Use AES-GCM, AES-CCM, or ChaCha20-Poly1305 instead.

checks.title: hashlib.md5() used on a password-shaped variable.
checks.remediation: hashlib.md5() used on a password-shaped variable. MD5 is broken for cryptographic use. Use a password-hashing function — bcrypt, scrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2 — never a raw hash.

checks.title: random module used inside a function whose name suggests a security-sensitive value ('$FN').
checks.remediation: random module used inside a function whose name suggests a security-sensitive value ('$FN'). The `random` module is NOT cryptographically secure. Use `secrets.token_urlsafe()`, `secrets.token_bytes()`, or `secrets.choice()` instead.

checks.title: hashlib.sha1() used on a password-shaped variable.
checks.remediation: hashlib.sha1() used on a password-shaped variable. SHA1 is unsuitable for password hashing (fast hash, no work factor). Use bcrypt, scrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2 instead.

checks.title: Django ORM raw SQL with a non-literal argument — SQL injection risk.
checks.remediation: Django ORM raw SQL with a non-literal argument — SQL injection risk. Pass user input as params, never interpolate into the query string. Prefer Django's ORM filter() expressions when possible.

checks.title: render_template_string() called with a non-literal template — server-side template injection (SSTI) risk.
checks.remediation: render_template_string() called with a non-literal template — server-side template injection (SSTI) risk. Use render_template() with a static .html file; never compose Jinja source from user input.

checks.title: Command execution with user-controlled input — command injection risk.
checks.remediation: Command execution with user-controlled input — command injection risk. Use subprocess.run() with a list of arguments and shell=False. Never pass user input directly to shell commands.

checks.title: eval()/exec() with dynamic argument — code injection risk.
checks.remediation: eval()/exec() with dynamic argument — code injection risk. Avoid eval/exec entirely. If required, validate input strictly against an allowlist before execution.

checks.title: pickle.loads() on a non-literal byte string — arbitrary code execution on deserialization.
checks.remediation: pickle.loads() on a non-literal byte string — arbitrary code execution on deserialization. Replace with json.loads() for untrusted input. If pickle is strictly required, sign the payload (hmac) and verify before unpickling.

checks.title: SQL query built via string formatting — SQL injection risk.
checks.remediation: SQL query built via string formatting — SQL injection risk. Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute("SELECT ... WHERE x = %s", (value,))

checks.title: subprocess with shell=True and a non-literal command — command injection risk.
checks.remediation: subprocess with shell=True and a non-literal command — command injection risk. Drop shell=True and pass argv as a list, OR shlex.quote() each interpolated argument if shell semantics are truly required.

checks.title: yaml.load() without yaml.SafeLoader can execute arbitrary Python code via the !!python/object tag.
checks.remediation: yaml.load() without yaml.SafeLoader can execute arbitrary Python code via the !!python/object tag. Use yaml.safe_load() or pass Loader=yaml.SafeLoader explicitly.

checks.title: AWS access-key ID literal detected in assignment to '$VAR'.
checks.remediation: AWS access-key ID literal detected in assignment to '$VAR'. Use the AWS SDK's credential provider chain (env vars, ~/.aws/credentials, instance role) instead of hardcoding. If the key is real, revoke it now.

checks.title: Inline GCP service-account JSON detected in assignment to '$VAR'.
checks.remediation: Inline GCP service-account JSON detected in assignment to '$VAR'. Load the credential from an external file via GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS or a secrets manager. Rotate the key in Google Cloud IAM immediately.

checks.title: Hardcoded database connection string with embedded credentials found in '$VAR'.
checks.remediation: Hardcoded database connection string with embedded credentials found in '$VAR'. Store connection strings in environment variables (e.g., DATABASE_URL). Rotate the database password immediately.

checks.title: Hardcoded secret found in assignment to '$KEY'.
checks.remediation: Hardcoded secret found in assignment to '$KEY'. Move secrets to environment variables or a secrets manager. Rotate the exposed credential immediately.

checks.title: PEM-encoded private key literal detected in assignment to '$VAR'.
checks.remediation: PEM-encoded private key literal detected in assignment to '$VAR'. Move the key out of source control immediately, rotate it on the server, and reload from disk or a secrets manager at runtime.

checks.title: Slack incoming-webhook URL hardcoded in '$VAR'.
checks.remediation: Slack incoming-webhook URL hardcoded in '$VAR'. Anyone with this URL can post into the bound channel. Rotate the webhook in Slack's app config and store the new URL in an env var (e.g. SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL).
